axes.purpose: Control sentence structure and grammatical choices accurately enough to understand, manipulate and independently produce school-level English.
includes: grammar structures required by the school programme
affirmative, negative and interrogative sentence control
tense and form choice from context
does_not_mean: memorising rule labels without successful production

axes.purpose: Understand and use the high-frequency vocabulary, chunks and collocations needed by the learner's school programme and target level.
includes: basic lexical precision needed for reading and writing
does_not_mean: isolated word-list memorisation as sufficient evidence
rare vocabulary used only to make tasks harder

axes.purpose: Understand short and progressively longer school-appropriate texts without relying on word-by-word translation.
does_not_mean: translation of every word before comprehension

axes.purpose: Produce comprehensible, task-appropriate written English with the organisation, grammar and vocabulary expected at the learner's school-year profile.
does_not_mean: accuracy scores that ignore whether the task was actually completed

axes.purpose: Understand level-appropriate spoken English well enough to identify gist, key detail and intended meaning in school-relevant listening tasks.
does_not_mean: artificially slow word-by-word audio as the only evidence

axes.purpose: Use English to perform practical communicative functions in written or spoken form when those functions are part of the school programme or recovery assessment.
includes: describing routines, people, places and plans
spoken interaction or oral response when required
does_not_mean: speaking being mandatory for every learner regardless of school requirements

cross_axis_rules: An assessment task may produce evidence for more than one competence axis, but each evidence claim must identify the primary axis and any secondary axes explicitly.
Italian-to-English translation is an assessment mode and may provide grammar, lexical and writing evidence; it is not itself a competence axis.
Mixed school assessment is an assessment mode and may sample several axes; it must not collapse those axes into one undifferentiated score.
No axis may be declared mastered solely from another axis's score.
